prompt:
Can you audit these two files for Google SEO problems before we launch? robots.txt is our live robots file and thank-you.html is served at https://www.brightkettle.example/checkout/thank-you . We want the checkout pages kept out of Google, and we want star ratings to show for the kettle we recommend on that page. Tell me what's actually broken vs nice-to-have.

Input files: robots.txt, thank-you.html
assertions: The audit points out that because /checkout/ is disallowed in robots.txt, Google cannot crawl the page and so cannot see its noindex tag, meaning the URL can still be indexed
The audit states that Google does not support the crawl-delay field in robots.txt
The audit states that a Noindex rule in robots.txt is not supported by Google
The audit states that the Sitemap line in robots.txt must be a fully qualified (absolute) URL
The audit states that the AggregateRating is missing a required count property (ratingCount or reviewCount)

The audit points out that the product rating marked up in the JSON-LD is not visible in the page content (or that the markup does not represent the main content of this page), which conflicts with Google's structured data guidelines
The audit clearly separates required fixes or violations from optional recommendations
The audit links to at least two developers.google.com documentation pages that back up its findings
